first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this saying 'Crete, Mum?' The first line says the questions now are practical ones: which month, which end of the island and what moves the cost. Those are my questions. No gushing about sunsets. I'll read it properly, top to bottom.

journey.quote: Temperatures are in degrees Celsius. Rain days are the average number of days in the month with measurable rain.
journey.reaction: Six columns of figures on the iPad is a lot to take in, and I had to scroll sideways. The paragraph underneath does the work for me though, so I skipped to that.

journey.quote: May and late September sit between those extremes.
journey.reaction: That's the answer I wanted. Mum doesn't cope with heat, so May or late September it is, as far as I'm concerned.

journey.section: Venue season windows and ceremony times
journey.quote: A late-afternoon ceremony in May leaves the evening open for a long dinner; a summer ceremony at half past six pushes the reception later into the night.
journey.reaction: Sensible. The older ones fade by ten, so an earlier ceremony suits our side of the family.

journey.quote: Heatwaves are frequent over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion and heat stroke, and many major tourist sites have little shade.
journey.reaction: Honest, and from the government, not a salesman. This is my real worry for Mum and my aunt, and it's said plainly without frightening me off the whole idea.

journey.quote: Smartraveller also advises comprehensive travel insurance, bought before you leave, that covers all medical costs overseas including evacuation, and notes that Greece sits in an active seismic zone, with earthquakes including near Crete.
journey.reaction: Earthquakes I hadn't thought of, and I'd rather know. The insurance advice is exactly what I'll be nagging everyone about. Good that it's here.

journey.quote: For a summer date, that means shade for the ceremony, water on every chair and a plan for the hottest hours.
journey.reaction: Practical. That's the kind of line that tells me someone has actually stood at one of these weddings.

journey.section: Choosing an area and a venue
journey.quote: Distances on Crete are real, and guests who land at one airport and stay at the other end will spend a good part of a day on the road.
journey.reaction: Thank you. I'd assumed it was a little island you could cross in an hour. A day in a car after 24 hours of flying would finish Mum off.

journey.quote: Couples who want every guest under one roof tend to look here first.
journey.reaction: Everyone under one roof sounds right for us, with older relatives. But under one roof isn't the same as getting from the room to the chapel. Are there steps? Is it a long walk? Nothing says.

journey.quote: A venue hired for the day, with no guest rooms on site, where you bring in your own caterer, furniture and suppliers.
journey.reaction: Lovely for the young ones, but who gets Mum back to her hotel at midnight from a hilltop garden? And bringing in our own caterer means more contracts with more people I've never met.

journey.section: Six venues from east to west
journey.quote: Not published: capacity or an exclusive-use option at St. Nicolas Bay, and capacity or a legal ceremony option at Caramel.
journey.reaction: I like that they admit what they don't know instead of filling the gap. Followed by someone confirming it in writing. That's how I'd want it done.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Abaton Island Resort & Spa ties every package to a minimum room booking for a minimum number of nights and a minimum reception size, and its packages do not include accommodation.
journey.reaction: Useful clause to know about, but where did Abaton come from? It isn't in the six venues. By now there's Elounda Collection, Abaton, Euphoria, Nana Princess, Minos Palace and I've lost track of which is which and where.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Euphoria Resort at Kolymvari sells complete packages whose items are not interchangeable: a service not used brings no refund or alternative, and amendments or custom packages cost extra.
journey.reaction: That's the sort of small print that catches people. Money we'd lose without noticing. Glad it's spelt out.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Its civil package rate does not include the Municipal fees, and its Orthodox rate does not include the Metropolis fee, so those are charged on top.
journey.reaction: Fees on top of the package. Exactly what I'd want flagged before anyone signs.

journey.quote: Put the same questions to each venue, and ask for the answers in writing.
journey.reaction: Ten good questions, in writing, I'll print them. But there's nothing about the deposit: how much, when, is it refundable, what if someone gets sick and we have to move the date. And nothing about whether an older guest can get to every space without steps.

journey.quote: 10. What happens on the day if weather or heat moves the ceremony indoors?
journey.reaction: Good. A plan B for the heat is exactly what I'd ask.

journey.quote: From Agios Nikolaos, Minos Beach Art Hotel puts Chania Airport at a 180-minute drive.
journey.reaction: Three hours. That settles which airport we fly into. Clear and useful.

journey.quote: Once on the island, most guests drive or take taxis.
journey.reaction: Mum isn't driving on Greek roads, and neither is my husband if I have anything to do with it. Is there a transfer anyone can organise, or a car that takes a walking frame? It just stops at taxis.

journey.quote: DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities accept only one issued in their own country, so ask whether you need one, where to get it and whether it needs an apostille.
journey.reaction: So does Crete accept the Australian one or not? I read it twice. It tells me to ask, which is fair, but I'd like to know who I'm asking.

journey.quote: Some couples marry legally at home and hold a symbolic ceremony on the island.
journey.reaction: That's what I'd suggest to them. Do the paperwork at the registry in Melbourne and enjoy Crete. Good that it's offered as a real option.

journey.quote: Three weeks before. Once the Municipality approves them, the originals are couriered to the hotel at your own cost at least 3 weeks before the wedding.
journey.reaction: Set out week by week, so my husband can put it in the diary. Much easier to follow than a block of text.

journey.quote: At the Elounda Collection, the couple registers the marriage at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days of the ceremony, with a Friday or weekend wedding registered the following Monday.
journey.reaction: A step after the wedding I'd never have known about. So they can't fly off on the Saturday. Good to know now, not later.

journey.section: Plan your Crete wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, in writing, in Australian dollars. That's most of what I want from whoever we pay. I'd still want to speak to them on the phone first.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues have step-free paths or lifts between rooms, the ceremony spot and the reception, for a guest with a walking frame?
What should we ask each venue about deposits: how much, when, whether it's refundable, and what happens if we have to move the date?
How do older guests who won't drive get from the airport to the venue, and back to their hotel late at night from a garden venue?
For Crete specifically, is the Australian-issued CNI accepted, or does it have to come from the embassy in Athens?
Who reads the venue contract if it's in Greek or priced in euros?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day, at 2am Greek time?
Is the first step a phone call with the Wedded Advisor before anything is booked or paid?

turn_offs_found.quote: Put the same questions to each venue, and ask for the answers in writing.
turn_offs_found.why: My turn-off is any planning advice that never mentions deposits or contracts. This article talks money for a whole section and gives ten questions, but the word 'deposit' doesn't appear once and there's no question about cancellation or moving the date. That's the first thing my husband will ask me, and it's the thing I'm most nervous about with an overseas supplier.

would_share_with: My husband, with the ten questions printed and 'what about the deposit?' written at the bottom
My sister, who is looking after Mum on the trip, with the heat, insurance and airport-distance paragraphs
My daughter, with the line about marrying legally at home and holding a symbolic ceremony on the island

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, start planning with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: Fee in writing, AUD quotes and one person start to finish is what I want. I'd click if I knew a real person would ring me before anything is booked, and could tell me which of these places Mum can actually get around.

top_3_changes: Add a deposit and cancellation question to the ten venue questions (how much, when, refundable, what if the date moves). It's the one money question the article never asks, and the first one a parent paying for it will.

Add access for older or less mobile guests: an eleventh question on step-free routes, lifts and distances between rooms, ceremony and reception, and a line in 'Getting around' on what guests who won't drive or take taxis should ask the venue about transfers.

In the costs section, say where Abaton, Euphoria, Nana Princess and Minos Palace are (east, centre or west) the first time each appears, so a reader on an iPad isn't left wondering which hotel is which.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad, mother uses a walking frame)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions only
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details, sourcing lines and absent prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator
Journey types limited to the allowed enum; every turn-off has a why

open_questions.question: Deposit and cancellation is absent from this article (it was question 10 in the Greece packages guide), and accessibility for elderly guests is again this persona's main content gap. Both can be added as venue questions without new venue facts. Treat as should-fix? Contract language, on-the-day contact and a phone-first step are business details and deferred.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised. The deposit point concerns which question to ask venues, not a figure.
